chunks.text: Black Measles (Esca) is a destructive, chronic grapevine trunk disease that attacks the vascular tissue (wood) of the vine. It restricts water and nutrient flow, leading to internal wood rot. The disease is notorious for remaining asymptomatic in the trunk for years before suddenly manifesting dramatic visual symptoms on leaves and fruit, often during the height of summer. It is considered one of the most severe threats to mature vineyards globally.

chunks.text: Black Rot is one of the most devastating fungal diseases of grapevines, particularly in regions with warm, humid, and rainy spring and summer weather. The fungus can infect all green, growing parts of the vine, including leaves, shoots, tendrils, and fruit. If left unmanaged, Black Rot can result in complete crop loss, as the fungus quickly rots the berries, turning them into hard, black, shriveled "mummies."

chunks.text: Isariopsis Leaf Spot is primarily a foliar disease that occurs in grape-growing regions characterized by warm, humid climates. It typically appears later in the growing season, often post-harvest or late summer. While it generally does not directly infect the grape berries or wood, severe infections can cause rapid and premature defoliation. This loss of foliage limits the vine's ability to photosynthesize, thereby reducing the accumulation of carbohydrate reserves needed for winter survival and robust shoot growth the following spring.

chunks.text: Early blight is a highly common fungal disease of tomatoes. Despite its name, it can occur at any time during the growing season. It primarily attacks older foliage first, slowly moving up the plant. While it rarely kills the plant outright, severe defoliation significantly reduces yield and exposes fruit to sunscald.

chunks.text: Late blight is one of the most destructive plant diseases known (the same pathogen responsible for the Irish Potato Famine). It is highly contagious and can completely destroy a tomato field within a few days under favorable weather conditions. It requires living host tissue to survive over winter in cold climates.
